label: Fintech Credit-Risk Assessment
description: Credit-risk assessment for fintech, alternative-data and embedded lending — cash-flow-based, behavioural and alt-data underwriting, thin-file / no-file populations, BNPL and embedded-finance exposures, alt-data model governance and fairness, and affordability under EBA/GL/2020/06 and CCD2 (EU) 2023/2225. The fintech variant of traditional credit risk.

claudeKnowledge.description: EBA Guidelines on Loan Origination and Monitoring (EBA/GL/2020/06); Consumer Credit Directive (EU) 2023/2225 (CCD2, transposition by 20 Nov 2025, application from 20 Nov 2026); CRR (EU) 575/2013 as amended by CRR3 (EU) 2024/1623; IFRS 9 expected-credit-loss staging; EBA ICAAP/ILAAP Guidelines (EBA/GL/2016/10) and SREP (EBA/GL/2022/03); EU AI Act (EU) 2024/1689 (high-risk creditworthiness systems, Annex III(5)(b)); GDPR (EU) 2016/679 Art. 22 automated decision-making; national consumer-credit transposition (Sweden Konsumentkreditlagen, FI guidance).

guidedInputs.label: Lending model / product
guidedInputs.description: Which fintech lending model is being assessed? This drives the relevant alt-data, affordability and concentration lenses.

guidedInputs.label: Entity & jurisdiction(s)
guidedInputs.description: Where is the lender authorised and where are the borrowers? Drives which transposition of CCD2 and which national caps apply.

guidedInputs.label: Underwriting data sources in use
guidedInputs.description: Which signals feed the credit decision? Each carries distinct governance, fairness and CCD2 Art. 18 data-quality obligations.

guidedInputs.label: Assessment focus areas
guidedInputs.description: Which dimensions should the assessment prioritise?

options.label: Fairness / bias / explainability (AI Act, GDPR Art. 22)

guidedInputs.label: Portfolio & business context
guidedInputs.description: Book size, vintages, approval rate, average ticket, observed loss/roll rates, funding structure.
guidedInputs.placeholder: e.g., €180M consumer instalment book, 14-month average tenor, 62% approval rate, 30+ DPD at 4.1% on the latest 6 vintages, funded via a €150M warehouse with a 8% first-loss tranche and a forward-flow buyer for the senior.

guidedInputs.label: Known issues or concerns
guidedInputs.description: Known model weaknesses, supervisory feedback, drift, complaints, or affordability gaps.
guidedInputs.placeholder: e.g., Open-banking categorisation degrades for gig-economy borrowers; the GBM score has not been revalidated since launch 14 months ago; BNPL affordability relies on soft signals only; a thematic FI review of consumer-credit affordability is expected this year.

exampleInput: We are a Nordic embedded-lending fintech offering BNPL and consumer instalment credit at merchant checkout across Sweden and Finland (~€180M book, average ticket €420, 14-month tenor). Underwriting is a gradient-boosted model fed by open-banking cash-flow categorisation, internal repayment behaviour, telco/utility history, and a thin bureau pull — roughly 35% of applicants are thin-file or new-to-credit. We're preparing for CCD2 application (BNPL now in scope) and an expected Finansinspektionen thematic review on affordability. Please assess our credit-risk and affordability framework: (1) is our affordability assessment defensible under EBA/GL/2020/06 and CCD2 Art. 18 given the alt-data inputs and thin-file population; (2) is the GBM model governance, validation and fairness posture adequate against the AI Act high-risk creditworthiness regime and GDPR Art. 22; (3) review IFRS 9 ECL staging for BNPL short-tenor exposures; and (4) flag concentration (top-5 merchants = 48% of originations) and the funding/liquidity interplay with our warehouse first-loss. Known weak spots: the model has not been revalidated since launch 14 months ago, and open-banking categorisation degrades for gig-economy income.

exampleValues.portfolio_context: €180M embedded BNPL + instalment book, average ticket €420, 14-month tenor, ~35% thin-file/new-to-credit, top-5 merchants = 48% of originations. Funded via a €150M warehouse with an 8% first-loss tranche and a forward-flow buyer for the senior.
exampleValues.known_concerns: GBM model not revalidated since launch 14 months ago. Open-banking categorisation degrades for gig-economy income. BNPL affordability relies on soft signals only. Expecting an FI thematic affordability review.
